Compute weekly proportion of population within regions

Source: R/region.R
migration_chronology.Rd

Given one or more species and a region (defined as an sf, sfc, or SpatVector polygon object), compute the proportion of each species' global modeled population (or the population within reference_region, if supplied) that falls within each region polygon for each of the 52 weeks of the year. The proportion-of-population raster data are downloaded automatically on first use.

Usage

migration_chronology(
  species,
  region,
  reference_region = NULL,
  resolution = c("27km", "9km", "3km"),
  bind_regions = FALSE,
  path = ebirdst_data_dir(),
  force = FALSE,
  show_progress = interactive()
)

Arguments

species

character; one or more species given as scientific names, common names, or six-letter species codes. Mixes of name types are accepted. The full list of valid species is in ebirdst_runs.

region

sf, sfc, or SpatVector; polygon features defining the region(s) of interest. Each feature is treated as a separate region.

reference_region

NULL, sf, sfc, or SpatVector; optional polygon defining the reference population relative to which proportions are calculated. If multiple features are present, they are unioned into a single polygon. When supplied, proportions are calculated for both region and reference_region, and proportion_population is computed as the proportion in region divided by the proportion in reference_region (returning 0 when both are 0, and NA when only the reference proportion is 0). This can be used, for example, to calculate continental proportions, such as the proportion of the North American population within the given region. Defaults to NULL (proportions are relative to the global modeled population).

resolution

character; resolution of the raster data: "27km" (default), "9km", or "3km". Note that the example dataset only provides 27 km data. If 9 km or 3 km data are requested for more than 25 species that require downloading, a warning is issued; in an interactive session confirmation is required before the downloads begin.

bind_regions

logical; if TRUE, all non-geometry attribute columns from region are appended to the output (ignored if region is an sfc object, which has no attributes). Defaults to FALSE.

path

character; directory to download the data to. All downloaded files will be placed in a sub-directory of this directory named for the data version year, e.g. "2020" for the 2020 Status Data Products. Each species' data package will then appear in a directory named with the eBird species code. Defaults to a persistent data directory, which can be found by calling ebirdst_data_dir().

force

logical; if the data have already been downloaded, should a fresh copy be downloaded anyway.

show_progress

logical; whether to print download progress information. Defaults to interactive(), so downloads are silent in non-interactive sessions (e.g. scripts and R Markdown).

Value

A data frame with one row per combination of species, week, and region polygon. Columns:

  • species_code: the alphanumeric eBird species code.

  • season: season the week falls within ("breeding", "nonbreeding", "prebreeding_migration", "postbreeding_migration", or "resident"), or NA if the week does not fall within a named season that passed expert review.

  • week: midpoint date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the week.

  • proportion_population: proportion of the species' global modeled population (or the population within reference_region, if supplied) within the region for that week. Computed as a weighted sum of proportion-of-population raster cells, where boundary cells are weighted by the fraction of the cell area covered by the polygon.

  • proportion_population_reference: proportion of the species' global modeled population within reference_region for that week. Only present when reference_region is supplied.

  • .region_number: integer (1-indexed) indicating which polygon in region the row corresponds to. Only present when region has more than one feature.

  • Additional columns from region if bind_regions = TRUE.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# download example data
ebirdst_download_status("yebsap-example")

# build a region polygon from the raster extent
rast <- load_raster("yebsap-example", "abundance", resolution = "27km")
region <- sf::st_as_sf(
  terra::as.polygons(terra::ext(rast), crs = terra::crs(rast))
)

chron <- migration_chronology("yebsap-example", region, resolution = "27km")
head(chron)
} # }
